comment: The checks that fail on purpose, declared once. Read by scripts/known-red.mjs (which asserts
they are STILL red and exits non-zero the day one passes), by the gated test scripts in
package.json (which exclude them from the steps that gate a merge), and by
tests/governance/known-red-gate.spec.ts (which holds all four consumers to this list).
Adding an entry here is not a way to silence a failing check. The only checks that belong are
ones whose evidence cannot be produced by an agent at all, and whose absence is itself the
record that the work is owed. Everything else red is a real failure.
Retiring an entry is not optional: the gate fails the build the moment its check passes, so
the check goes back into the suite that gates merges and a later malformed record fails again.

checks.owes: T885 (EPIC-029) — a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass, recorded as a transcript naming the reader, its version, a journey and a date
checks.why: An agent cannot hear a screen reader or see whether focus order and announcements are meaningful. A record claiming otherwise would fabricate the evidence the check exists to test for.

checks.owes: T999t (EPIC-035) — the Tier 2 defect-room journey, all seven steps: report, triage, reproduce, failing test, repair tasks, verify, close
checks.why: The journey is keyboard-only against a running application, and two of its seven steps refuse in this deployment because RepairTaskPort and TestExecution are unbound. Typing the transcript is the fabrication the check exists to test for.
